quick.summary: Why live data acts differently than historical data.
quick.takeaway: Compare live numbers to past data to catch hidden differences.

parts.title: Find The Information Gap

beats.line: My model passed all tests yesterday. Why is it failing live today?
Think of a doctor looking at an old health file.
They might miss a brand new symptom.
Right. What they read does not match the person sitting there.
Your model trained on neat historical data in a warehouse.
But live in the world, the data looks slightly different.
We call this training serving skew.
Can I just call it an information gap?
How does this gap actually happen in our systems?

parts.cliff: The hidden differences between past and present.

beats.line: It happens when the live system calculates things differently.
But we use the exact same logic for both.
The logic might be the same, but the timing changes.
Your past data had all day to count daily visits.
And the live system has to count them instantly.
Exactly. The live system might miss the last few minutes.
To fix it, you log the live data and compare it.
I see. I check if the live numbers match the old numbers.

quiz.question: What is a common cause for an information gap between training and live data?
options: The timing of the calculations differs.
The live system is fully offline.
The past data was totally faked.
The model forgets how to multiply.
quiz.explanation: Even with the same logic, systems calculate live events on a different schedule than batch jobs.

quiz.question: Using the exact same logic guarantees the live data will match the past data.
quiz.explanation: Timing and missing inputs can still create differences, even if the math logic is identical.
